title: add jsonschema strict-mode improved error messages + OpenAI compat for response_format
author: Ben Thompson
description: Motivation: enable a robust, developer-friendly strict-mode for JSON Schema-based structured output (response_format) while preserving OpenAI compatibility and surfacing actionable error messages when generation fails validation. This PR implements stricter validation paths in the API surface, richer error payloads for downstream SDKs, and a compatibility shim to maintain behavior for existing OpenAI-compat clients. Summary of changes: Adds a new 'strict_mode' flag to response_format handling that enforces schema validation of model outputs. When strict_mode is enabled the runtime performs post-token validation and returns structured error objects in a consistent format instead of best-effort outputs. Introduces improved error codes and human-readable messages, plus a new 'validation_hints' array for common fixes (e.g., missing required fields, type mismatches, enum violations). Adds OpenAI-compat layer handling so clients using the compatibility mode receive errors in the expected 'error' envelope while still including our extended 'validation' metadata. Compatibility & migration: Default behavior is unchanged (strict_mode=false). Customers who opt into strict_mode may need to add retry or fallback logic in their callers; the release_notes include suggested guidance. OpenAI-compat clients will continue to get the legacy error envelope but we augment it with 'x-redwood-validation' metadata when running in OpenAI compatibility mode. Implementation details: Runtime: adds a validation step after token emission that uses the existing jsonschema validator (upgraded to v4) with a fast-fail path for common schema patterns. API layer: extends the response_format protobuf/JSON contract with a new boolean 'strict_mode' flag and an opaque 'validation_profile' string for advanced tuning. Errors: introduces canonical error codes: VALIDATION_ERROR, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, SCHEMA_TIMEOUT, CAST_ERROR. Each error includes 'message', 'path' (JSONPath as string), and optional 'validation_hints' (list of short strings). OpenAI compat shim wraps these into an 'error' object with code/message and adds 'x-redwood-validation' for the extra fields. Tests & CI: unit tests for validator logic, integration test covering streaming + strict_mode where we verify the runtime cancels the stream and returns a structured error. Added e2e test to redwood-openai-compat to validate the compatibility envelope. Benchmarks: measured median extra latency of ~6ms per request for schema validation on small schemas; added a microbenchmark and guard to opt-out heavy validation via 'validation_profile'. Docs & examples: updated redwood-docs with examples showing strict_mode usage and suggested fallback patterns. Added examples to SDKs demonstrating how to surface validation_hints to application logic. Follow-ups: (1) telemetry to track strict_mode adoption and common validation_hints. (2) optional 'auto-repair' mode to attempt minimal fixes on common enum/type issues (design doc in ENG-1879).
commits: feat(api): add strict_mode flag and response_format validation hook
feat(openai-compat): map validation errors into compat envelope
test: add unit/integration tests for strict validation
docs: add strict_mode examples and migration guidance
review_comments: Asha: Can you clarify the performance impact for larger schemas? Suggest adding a guard for worst-case runtimes.
Ben: Added microbenchmark and a 'validation_profile' opt-out knob; documented the measured median overhead (~6ms) and recommended using profiles for large schemas.
Miguel: For OpenAI compat, ensure the error fields are stable; we should use 'x-redwood-validation' as the stable key rather than ad-hoc fields.
Ben: Updated compat_shim to always include 'x-redwood-validation' with a compact summary and optional full 'validation' object when requested via query param.
Claire: Tests look good; suggest adding an integration case for streaming where validation fails mid-stream.
Ben: Added integration test that simulates a model producing invalid JSON mid-stream; runtime cancels remaining tokens and returns PARTIAL_OUTPUT with path info.
release_notes: Added optional response_format.strict_mode to enforce JSON Schema validation on generated outputs. When enabled, the API will return structured validation errors (VALIDATION_ERROR, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, SCHEMA_TIMEOUT, CAST_ERROR) with human-readable messages and validation_hints. Default behavior unchanged. See docs for migration guidance and fallback patterns.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps strict_mode opt-in to avoid breaking existing workflows. Telemetry hooks were added to monitor adoption. We should follow up with a small rollout to a subset of customers via feature flags.
example_error_payload: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Output did not match schema: missing required property 'email'","x-redwood-validation":{"path":"$.user","validation_hints":["add 'email' string field","ensure 'user' object includes 'email'"]}}}
migration_guidance:
- Default: no action required.
- To opt-in: set response_format.strict_mode=true in create response request.
- Handle VALIDATION_ERROR by inspecting x-redwood-validation.validation_hints and either retrying with a corrected prompt or falling back to non-strict mode.
- OpenAI-compat clients will receive errors in the legacy envelope with x-redwood-validation metadata.
